verdict:
NOT READY TO BUILD: the evidence work is good, but the SDF recipe fails several of its own probes, and the probes cannot detect the artefact the spec is meant to replace. I checked A15 read-only on engine\packs\felid\features\spec_eyes.json, in 6 min (unix 1792325178 to 1792325515). The only output is scratch in %TEMP%\p2prep_check-eyes\sdfcheck.py, run with Blender 5.2's Python at under 50 MB. Free RAM was 4.9 GB.

What holds up:
- The globe arithmetic checks out: sag 5.70, RS 9.45, apex 10.30 mm in front of the sclera centre, and the L apex is reproduced from the centre plus the axis.
- Units and the head frame are consistent.
- OPEN Phase 1 numbers are handled as PHASE1_SUMMARY directs: B1 2.0-2.4 is used and the 0.5 is rejected; B2 overhang and S1 64-69 are used and 75-78 is rejected; the S2 slant spread is used.
- No Tripo nostril, whisker or cap geometry is copied. The cap is explicitly not copied.
- J2 is respected: the lower lid is taken from the photo.

Coverage of the person's additions:
- C6b and C14 are ears-only, so they do not apply here.
- C13 is relevant through the supraorbital whiskers, and it is not covered (see should-fix).
blocking: Recipe step 5 has the rounding offset with the wrong sign. The cut term -(M+o*c+0.45) followed by Lid_r = Lid-0.45 GROWS the lid instead of eroding then dilating it. Checked numerically: the lid's inner face reaches h = -0.30..-0.45, so it sits 0.4 mm INSIDE the globe, which is C6's planted failure 'lids cut through the globe'. The free edge lands at M = -0.90 at the globe and -1.30 at the top, so the opening loses about 1.8 mm of height (14.0 down to about 12.2 mm), undoing the photo's k_low 1.18. The lid top sits at h 2.35 instead of 1.9. As written, the build fails the spec's own crease (+-0.5), fissure-height, no-penetration and lid-height probes. Fix: erode the shell and the cut by 0.45 before the -0.45, or round only the anterior edge.

Recipe steps 6 and 7 run in the wrong order. The socket (S2 = smax(S1, 0.05-G)) is carved BEFORE the lids are unioned (S3 = smin(S2, Lid_r, k=1.0)). So neither the lid nor the k=1.0 smooth-min bulge (up to k/4 = 0.25 mm of extra material) is kept out of the globe. Carve the socket last: S_final = smax(S3, 0.05-G, k).

Recipe step 8 does not bound the third eyelid. TEL = max(|h-0.35|-0.3, Cr, M-4, -M-6), and Cr only removes one disk of radius 6 mm; nothing confines the membrane to the medial canthus. Measured on the outline_UV polygons, TEL covers 51 % of the L opening (119 of 232 mm2, 87 mm2 of it lateral of U = +2 mm) and 50 % of R (113 of 225 mm2), i.e. a membrane over the lateral cornea. The third-eyelid probes look only at the medial canthus (exposed width 0.5 +-0.3; the pale wedge), so they would PASS this. Bound it (for example distance from Pmed < 3-4 mm, matching the text's '~3 mm lower / ~1.5 mm upper') and add a probe on the exposed TEL area or extent, or on the share of the opening where cornea is visible.

No probe fails on the artefact the spec replaces: a lid fused to the eye surface instead of a fold resting on a separate globe. (1) The 'globe is a separate closed manifold' probe counts skin vertices with M > 0.5 and G < 0. A globe unioned into the skin has no such vertices, so it PASSES, even though the spec's own do-not list forbids that union. (2) The 'no gap and no penetration' probe takes lid inner-face vertices with M in [0,4]. A fused lid, or Tripo's ridge, has none, so the probe passes vacuously. Needed: the globe is its own closed connected component; a minimum count of inner-face samples per station over the 4 mm fornix; a rotate-the-globe +-15 deg clearance test (the stated reason for the fornix); and planted failures (union, fused lid) that each probe must fail. The spec defines a plant only for the overhang probe, against A10 / Round 0.

The spec knowingly breaks approved criterion C3 and resets it without asking. Its own cornea_vs_tripo_cap says the cornea stands 1.15-1.23 mm (p10 1.34-1.45) IN FRONT of Tripo's surface. C3 requires the furless eye to sit ON the envelope within +-0.5 mm, and C3b says the eyes must not bulge. The evidence_ranking 'exception' puts cited anatomy above Tripo, inverting G3, and open_and_conflicts then redefines C3 to be measured 'against OUR globe'. No probe reports apex-to-envelope distance; the C3b probe only looks 3-13 mm outside the crease. The photo cannot see depth here, so this is a judgement call. It needs the person's or orchestrator's ruling (r 8.82 cornea proud of the envelope, versus apex on the envelope with the margin about 1.7 mm off the globe, or a compromise) before build, plus a probe that reports the chosen offset.
should: The photo's inner dark rim was back-projected as the CREASE, but under the spec's own lid model the visible rim is the lid edge's outline. That edge leans o = 0.4 mm (1.0 mm medially) over the globe, and a 1.9 mm wall seen about 14 deg off-axis adds about 0.47 mm of parallax. So the crease is placed about 0.4-0.9 mm too far into the opening, and the photo-outline probe (tol 1.5 px = 0.55 mm) will probably fail. Re-derive the crease by rendering the lid model through the camera, or state which quantity the photo fixes.

Lean against crease angle: o = 0.4 ramped over h 0-1.2 gives an interior angle of atan(1.2/0.4) = 71.6 deg mid-lid. That is outside the spec's own 66 +-5. Medial (o = 1.0) gives 50 deg; lateral (0.6) gives 63 deg. Ramp over about 0.9 mm, or set o about 0.53, to hit 66.

The 0.45 mm round is applied to the whole free edge, including the posterior edge that sits on the globe. Anatomically the posterior lid margin is a sharp edge against the globe. A fillet there lifts the contact point about 0.3 mm and spoils the 0-0.8 mm chord crease-angle probe. Round only the anterior edge.

The angular coordinates U = R*atan2(q.u,q.n), V = R*atan2(q.v,q.n) are not isotropic. On the diagonal at the canthal angle (62 deg) a true 10.23 mm arc reads 12.38 mm (+21 %); at the fornix (87 deg), 14.35 reads 20.0 mm. The 'mm' are also at the globe radius, not at height h. So every M-distance (overhang 0.4, round 0.45, fornix 4, fade 6, TEL 0.5) is distorted at oblique stations. Use true polar (theta, phi) with arc R*theta, or a 3-D distance to the margin curve.

C13 is not covered. The superciliary (supraorbital) whiskers ('a few long hairs over each eye', Mivart 1881, in cat-hair-streams.md) appear in no feature spec; I grepped all four specs. The eye spec should define their follicle root zone above the medial upper lid, kept clear of the lid fold and periocular coat edits, or hand them off explicitly. The same applies to the 'first row of skin hairs' that stands in for lashes.

Two probes cannot tell the replacement from Tripo:
- The corneal-highlight probe's tolerance (5 px, about 1.9 mm) is wider than the gap between r 8.82 and Tripo's r about 14.7 cap (highlight offset about 1.5 mm, about 4 px). Compute the expected spot for both and tighten.
- The third-eyelid 'Lab L > 135' probe means nothing on a Stage 3 clay render. Move it to Stage 4 and keep a geometric check for Stage 3.

Photo scale: the spec measures 0.367-0.381 mm/px at the eyes; my check of the eye spacing gives about 0.39. PHASE2_ROUND0 bases its photo tolerance on '~0.27 mm/px'. Reconcile the two so the px tolerances map correctly to mm.

Registration: the fissure-midpoint registration partly uses the fissure to place Tripo in the photo. It is fine for size (k_low) but circular for position. Say so, or register on non-eye landmarks (ears, chin, nose), which the spec itself lists as not done.

Interface: coat_field.py's eye_opening and periocular masks still use the Phase 1 margin while the skin rebuild is running now. The lower-lid band (0.5-1.3 mm) will get coat depth. The spec notes this, but nobody owns the fix. Route it to the skin agent or the orchestrator; the 0-1 mm-band depth probe will catch it at fur time.
